_comment: Prompt templates per class. Every template is encoded with the VLM text
encoder and the embeddings are averaged per class to form the class-generic
E_i is used in three places:
1. the frozen class-generic token inside every DIPT prompt (stage 1),
3. the text target of the original (non-DIPT) RISE distance loss.
'templates' feeds the aggregated embedding; 'handcrafted' is the single
prompt per class used by the one-prompt zero-shot baseline and by the
camelyon17 templates are reproduced verbatim from the original
'normal' is a single string there: the original source omitted two commas,
so three intended prompts were concatenated by Python. It is kept as-is so
the aggregated embedding matches the published runs - split it into three
separate entries if you prefer the evident intent.
kather19 has no counterpart in the original code; those templates are new.
